html:
Lilongwe became the capital of Malawi in 1975, replacing Zomba, the colonial capital in the south, as part of a plan by Hastings Banda to develop the central region.

Banda came from the centre, and the move shifted power and investment toward the Chewa heartland. South Africa, then an ally, helped pay for the new city, with government buildings on a planned site called Capital Hill.

Lilongwe has grown into the largest city in Malawi, the seat of government and the centre of the tobacco trade. Blantyre in the south remains the commercial centre. The capital reflects Banda's shaping of the country, and the Chewa heartland around it.
sum: Lilongwe became the capital of Malawi in 1975, replacing Zomba, the colonial capital in the south, as part of a plan by Hastings Banda to develop the central region.
